methodological_rigor.justification: Phase 2, single-arm, open-label design with 26 evaluable participants. No control group or randomization; open-label design limits internal validity and causality inference. Sample size informed qualitatively for safety assessment but not formally powered for efficacy. Baseline characteristics presented; comparison to ZUMA-1 is descriptive without matching. Statistical analysis uses appropriate descriptive methods and Kaplan-Meier estimation but no formal hypothesis testing or multiplicity correction.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Phase 2 single-arm trial (LoE 4) addressing unmet need: CD19-negative relapse in ~30% of axi-cel responders. Direct clinical relevance demonstrated by high CR rate (73%) and durable 24-month PFS (48.2%), exceeding ZUMA-1 monotherapy outcomes. Dual CD19/CD20 targeting approach has immediate translational implications for mitigating antigen escape in chemorefractory large B cell lymphoma.

reporting_quality.justification: Open-label single-arm phase 2 trial; CONSORT not strictly applicable but key reporting elements present. Methods clearly describe study design, participant flow (Figure 1), endpoints per Lugano classification, safety assessments with CTCAE grading, and comprehensive pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic evaluations. Data availability not explicitly stated beyond trial registry (NCT04002401); no commitment to share raw data or biospecimens.

novelty_literature.justification: Dual-targeting approach of axi-cel plus rituximab to mitigate CD19 antigen escape is hypothesis-driven and grounded in preclinical evidence. However, study is largely descriptive without definitive demonstration of synergy or mechanistic validation. Authors acknowledge critical limitation: only 1 paired biopsy at relapse obtained, precluding investigation of antigen escape mechanisms. Represents meaningful extension of CAR-T strategy but lacks mechanistic depth.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear structure, comprehensive methods section, and detailed results. Figures (especially pharmacokinetic profiles and biomarker analyses) effectively communicate findings. Discussion appropriately contextualizes ZUMA-14 within ZUMA-1 and acknowledges limitations. Writing is precise and publication-ready despite exploratory nature of study.

key_strengths: High CR rate (73%) with durable 24-month PFS (48.2%) exceeding axi-cel monotherapy historical controls
Comprehensive mechanistic characterization including pharmacokinetics, cytokine/chemokine profiling, and MRD by ctDNA
Exploratory biomarker analyses identifying NK cell infiltration and transcriptomic signatures associated with ongoing response
Acceptable safety profile with no grade 3+ CRS and manageable neurologic events despite dual targeting
Practical, feasible approach addressing real clinical problem of antigen escape in CAR-T therapy
key_concerns: Open-label, single-arm design without control group limits causality inference and assessment of true synergy between axi-cel and rituximab
Small sample size (n=26) with limited statistical power; no formal hypothesis testing or multiplicity correction for exploratory analyses
Critical mechanistic limitation: only 1 paired biopsy at relapse obtained, preventing investigation of CD19/CD20 antigen escape as intended
Descriptive comparison to ZUMA-1 confounded by unmatched baseline characteristics (participants in ZUMA-14 had lower risk, less heavy pretreatment)
Lack of clear evidence that rituximab provides synergistic benefit beyond rituximab monotherapy; clinical improvements may reflect lower-risk population
Demographics not representative (73% white), limiting generalizability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 assignment reflects exploratory phase 2 design with promising clinical signals but insufficient methodological rigor for higher consideration. Single-arm design and absence of mechanistic validation of dual-targeting benefit preclude Tier 2; however, novel approach and clinical outcomes support Tier 3 exploratory acceptance pending prospective validation.
